source: Vincent Design Project Accessibility Sheets template (WCAG 2.2)

guidance.text: Check if it's our responsibility or the client's to be writing alternative content. Regardless, it needs to have been written and entered into the CMS according to standards.
Types of content that require on-page (visible) alternatives should have designs that facilitate this.
All types of content requiring text alternatives have a field for it in the CMS and that it's being output correctly.
Check if it's our responsibility or the client's to be writing alternative content. Sufficient alternative content (usually a transcript) must be provided when the content uses only one sense.
Make sure the design thoughtfully includes and plans for the chosen alternative content.
Correctly link the alternative content with the audio-only or video-only media.
If it's our responsibility to be writing captions, they need to be written. Regardless, check that captions are written accurately and timed correctly in the platform.
The design must allow for a video player that has caption features.
Captions are running when toggled on and are visible (contrast is sufficient).

If we are going with the media alternative, check if it's our responsibility or the client's. If it's ours, the transcript* must be written according to accepted standards. If we are going with described audio, this falls onto the video provider.

If were are not going with the media alternative, and it's in scope and our responsibility: Make sure there is at least one version of the video with, or, availability of, a synchronized spoken description of the visual content.

If we are going with the media alternative, check if it's our responsibility or the client's. If it's ours, the transcript* must be made available in the design somewhere. If we are going with described audio, make sure we design for the link to the video with the audio description.
If it's in scope and our responsibility: Make sure there is at least one version of the video with, or, availability of, a synchronized spoken description of the visual content.
Design for a link out to the version of the video containing the audio description.
When authoring content, semantic elements need to be chosen according to standards. Things like heading order, table structure, and using elements as they are intended for, are of note.
Inputs have their labels correctly linked/associated, the most semantic element possible is chosen for the content, landmarks are used and labelled, icon font <span>'s are identified correctly.
Make sure whitespace is not used as a substitution for CSS styling. Things like not using whitespace to create columns, tables, or increased letter spacing.
Designs across breakpoints should not shift order wherever possible.
DOM order of elements across all breakpoint should retain their meaning especially when linearized.
Instructions can't rely on senses. Think content order (before, after, heading names, etc.) vs visual positioning (left, right, sidebar, etc.).
Page orientation cannot be locked. Mobile phones for example should be able to rotate and the site should still work.
Autofill values should be used for fields wherever possible.
Use more than just colour (e.g. words in copy, graph/chart legends, states) to convey meaning.
Use more than just colour (e.g. words in copy, graph/chart legends, states) to convey meaning.
No audio should really be playing automatically unless absolutely required.
If audio is automatically playing for more than 3 seconds, a way to stop or pause the audio must be available.
Check that the pause/stop feature functions as expected.

Check that all text foreground and background colours pass the appropriate contrast ratio minimums. Pay special attention to text over images. Sample the lightest and darkest part of the entire image against the text. Recommended Tool.

Check that all text foreground and background colours pass the appropriate contrast ratio minimums. Pay special attention to text over images. Sample the lightest and darkest part of the entire image against the text. Recommended Tool.
Plan for all text to be allowed to increase to 200% without getting cut off within containers/design elements.
Set the browser's base font setting to "32px" or something equivalent. Test to see if all content remains legible and functional.
Images of text should almost always be converted to proper page copy.
Images of text should almost always be converted to proper page copy.
You can check for copy that has line breaks that make copy nonsensical when the line breaks are treated as pauses.
Take care not to contain text within small boundaries, and allow it to flow onto as many lines as possible.
Check that at 400% zoom, 320 "browser px" wide screen size, all text and content is legible and does not cause a horizontal scrollbar.
Check that all UI and graphic colours pass the appropriate contrast ratio minimums. Pay special attention UI elements over images, and color-coded graphics. Recommended Tool.
Check that all UI and graphic colours pass the appropriate contrast ratio minimums. Pay special attention UI elements over images, and color-coded graphics. Recommended Tool.
Test the page using the recommended bookmarklet. Text must be legible and complete.
Generally, content should have a more clear trigger than focus and hover, but if it must use one of the two, make sure to design for the criterion's requirements.
Make sure the content that becomes visible on focus or hover follows the criterion's requirements.
Anything that uses a pointer/mouse to control should have visible on-screen controls as an alternative, like prev/next buttons for a slider.
All features should be functional via the keyboard and should follow the expected patterns for the element type.
The keyboard alone must be able to navigation through all the elements without getting stuck in a loop.
Shortcuts shouldn't use printable keys only.
Shortcuts shouldn't use printable keys only.
Check for any time limits set by the content, and design the appropriate mecahnism to disable or extend.
Check for any automatically moving content (more than 5 seconds) and assess if it's necessary. If it is, we need to design a mecahnism to pause, stop, or hide it.
Videos should not contain flashing content.
Indicate areas of repeated navigational content for developers.
Any repeated navigation content should have a functioning bypass link to skip the repeated content. Test to make sure it's working and coded correctly.
Page titles (not H1) should describe the page topic or purpose as concisely as possible.
Make sure the page title is automated and set correctly.
Take care to pay attention to the order of focusable elements in that the DOM order makes sense with the visual order.
Check that the focus order matches the DOM order so that the focus is not "jumping" around the page.
Written links need to have its text describe the link destination. Images that are links should also follow this rule, the image's alt text needs to describe the link destination.

Check if the link text alone describes the link destination. Otherewise, indicate to the developer what the context should be (previous paragraph, a heading nearby, etc.) You may need to collaborate with the content team.
Make sure additional programmatic contexts are coded correctly.
Advising which ways of accessing content for a project may be helpful. There must not be any orphan pages.
Design for the decided multiple ways of accessing content.

Headings should not generally be more than a few words in order to describe the content section. When elements have labels, they should descripe the purpose for that element. Example: A first name field's label is "first name" instead of "first".
Headings should appear before the content it's a heading for, and not after. The headings were written to describe the following content's purpose or topic and so it must be preserved.
You may design custom focus indicators for some, or all elements. Please ensure they follow standards. At the very least, we must use the browser default focus rings.
Any focusable element must have a visible focus state that is the default or better than default (see standards).
An element in focus cannot be completely covered (or have the potential to be completely covered) by anything like a mobile menu or modal.

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.canned: No multi-point or path-based gestures were found on the website.

guidance.text: Do not require multipoint (multi-finger) gestures or path-based gestures (where path of travel is important) for content operation.
Do not require multipoint (multi-finger) gestures or path-based gestures (where path of travel is important) for content operation.
Do not use the "down" event for any trigger, only the "up".
Make sure the accessible name matches the visible name/label (at least the first part).
Motion controls are not the only way to operate content.
Any dragging movement for operating content also has visible button-based controls.
Dragging must not be the only way to operate content.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.canned: Target sizes were found to be larger than the minimum.

guidance.text: Targets must be 24 by 24 CSS pixels unless they are spaced far enough apart (check criterion for rules).
The language of the overall HTML document, and each iFrame containing a new HTML document must be identified.
Each language change (according to the standards) should be identified using the language tag.
Each language change (according to the standards) should be identified using the language tag.
No element receiving focus should be initiating a context change in any circumstance.
Inputs that change the page context need to have content explaining the behavior ahead of time.
Check that inputs changing context have sufficient notice that is programmatically available.
Repeated navigational elements need to be in the same relative order each time they appear on a page. Things like table of contents, manual next/previous post links, etc, are things to watch.
Repeated navigational elements need to be in the same relative order each time they appear on a page. Things like table of contents, manual next/previous post links, etc, are things to watch.
Repeated navigational elements need to be in the same relative order each time they appear on a page. Things like table of contents, manual next/previous post links, etc, are things to watch.
Links to the same destination across different pages need to be labelled the same way.
Take care that links, labels, and buttons are labelled the same way each time if they do the same thing or go to the same destination.

Links to the same destination across different pages need to be labelled the same way. Take care that links, labels, and buttons are labelled the same way each time if they do the same thing or go to the same destination.
Any "help" mechanisms are in the same spot on every page.
Any "help" mechanisms are in the same DOM order on every page.
Error display can be designed. Inline vs before/after form vs modal, and appearance can all be customized (depending on form provider) if desired.
Check that any error detected (even if it is auto-corrected) has text displayed on the page to describe it. Content and method does not matter here.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.canned: Labels are provided for all required user input

guidance.text: Content requiring user input needs to have instructions (labels are instructions) that concicely explain the input requirement.
Content requiring user input needs to have visible instructions (labels are instruction) in a predictable position.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.canned: Fields requiring a specific format have the format suggestion in the error message.

guidance.text: Overall tone and voice for the error messages can be guided to the developer with sample copy of error messages. You may also want to review error messages for following the copy style guide.
Each error message, when corrections are known, should have the suggestions outlined in the text.
Forms (including checkouts) that fall into this criteria should have a comprehensive checkbox or confirmation that needs to be accepted before submission. This copy should follow the standards.
Form fields that were previously asked for entry should not be asked again. If they need to be, consult with the developer to check for feasibility.
Duplicated fields should have the previously entered information automatically populated into the repepated fields.
Do not require cognitive tests (including some reCAPTCHA's) for forms. Consult with the project developer on more appropriate security measures.
Make sure any spam reduction measures are through things like honeypots and invisible reCAPTCHA's instead of cognitive testing.
Any custom components outside of default HTML5 must be run past development in order to check for feasibility.

Avoid custom HTML "components" like the plague. Otherwise, you must test them using keyboard, pointer, and screen reader expected beahviors for the component type. Use semantic and default HTML5 elements 99% of the time.
Anything considered a "status message" must be run past development in order to check for feasibility.
Anything considered a "status message" must be marked up correctly and tested using a screen reader.
